styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Zhongyang Dajie, St Sophia and the Ice Festival.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Harbin sausage, hotpot and Russian-influenced bakeries.

styles.label: Family
styles.blurb: Ice sculptures, sledding and Sun Island in the snow.

stays.why: Walk to the pedestrian street, St Sophia Cathedral and riverside. Easiest base for first-timers.
Cheap, handy for trains and the metro; a short taxi to the old town sights.
Older streets, local food and markets; good value and a real neighbourhood feel.
Close to Sun Island and the Ice and Snow World site; quieter, but you need taxis or the metro to the centre.

food: Try Harbin red sausage (红肠) and Russian-style bread from old bakeries near Zhongyang Dajie.
Hotpot and barbecue are winter staples; expect ¥60–150 per person.
Guobaorou (sweet-and-sour pork) is a local classic; look for busy family restaurants in Daowai.
Winter street snacks: frozen pears, candied hawthorn skewers and roasted sweet potatoes, ¥5–20.
Ice cream and cold noodles are popular even in winter; check hygiene at small street stalls.
more_time: Add a day trip to the Siberian Tiger Park north of the river; check opening hours on the day.
In summer, take the Songhua River ferry to Sun Island for parks and walks.
Swap one city day for the Russian-influenced architecture around St Sophia and the old Jewish quarter.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the Ice Festival or summer riverfront, the old streets and a food evening without rushing.

month_notes: January: deepest winter, highs near -12°C. Ice Festival season; dress in layers.
February: still very cold, around -6°C. Ice sites may close late in the month; check on the day.
March: warming to about 5°C but icy underfoot. Few crowds.
April: mild days near 14°C, cool nights. Good for walking the old streets.
May: pleasant at 21°C; rain picks up. Bring a light jacket.
June: warm at 25°C with frequent rain. Parks are green.
July: hottest month, around 28°C and humid. Plan indoor breaks.
August: warm and wet, about 25°C. Sun Island is at its best.
September: comfortable at 21°C; a good shoulder month.
October: cooling to 12°C. Crisp air, fewer visitors.
November: near 0°C and windy. Ice sites not yet open; check dates.
December: cold at -10°C. Ice Festival usually opens late in the month; book early.

climate_guide.summary: Long, very cold winters and short, warm, rainy summers. Winter is the headline season; summer is green and humid.

items.title: Winter is the draw
items.text: December to February highs sit between -12°C and -6°C. The Ice and Snow Festival runs in this window; check exact dates.

items.title: Pack for real cold
items.text: Thermal layers, a heavy down coat, hat, gloves and boots with grip. Wind makes it feel colder than the numbers.

items.title: Summer is wet
items.text: June to August brings 14–15 rain days a month. Carry an umbrella and plan indoor backups.

items.title: Best shoulder months
items.text: May and September are mild and drier, around 21°C highs. Good for walking and river trips.

items.title: Short daylight in winter
items.text: Days are short in December and January. Do outdoor sights in the morning and early afternoon.

items.title: Watch your footing
items.text: Ice and packed snow make pavements slippery from November to March. Grippy boots help.

transit.best: Metro for main sights; taxis or Didi for short hops, especially in winter cold.

modes.text: Lines 1, 2 and 3 run 06:00–21:00; fares ¥2–5. Good for reaching the centre and Songbei.
Buses cover most of the city; fares ¥1–2, pay by IC card or cash.
Taxis are cheap; ask for the meter (请打表) and expect a ¥1 fuel surcharge. Didi works too; taxis often stop for extra passengers at peak.
Not advised for short visits; traffic is dense and signage is mostly Chinese.
Fine around Zhongyang Dajie and the old town. In winter, ice makes pavements slippery.
Summer ferries cross the Songhua River to Sun Island; tickets sold at the dock.
